---
title: "Tests and verification"
---

Ask for executable evidence, not reassurance. A focused test or **data contract** (rules the data must satisfy) should fail for the known defect and pass after the repair. A reviewer should understand it. Also inspect tables, figures, manifests, warnings, and uncertainty. Passing code does not prove the interpretation.

Check uniqueness, referential integrity, allowed values, missingness rules, row counts, seeds, and file hashes as needed. Run a small **smoke test** (a quick check that the main path works). Ask for the command and output, then run the check yourself when it matters.

Project instructions may ask agents to distinguish observation from inference. Keep that rule only if it improves their work.
